transfers.source_mechanism: Hydrophilic gel matrix at high concentration generates osmotic pressure to retain fluid against evaporative forces, with temporal aperture regulation reducing loss during high-evaporation periods.
transfers.target_problem:
Battery Electrolyte Design

Need: electrolyte for lithium-ion battery with wider temperature range (-40 to 80C) and higher ionic conductivity (target: 10 mS/cm). Current electrolytes use LiPF6 in organic carbonates. Must be electrochemically stable (4.5V window), non-flammable, and compatible with graphite anode and NMC cathode.
transfers.transferred_principle: A stimuli-responsive polymer matrix generates a Donnan potential/swelling pressure to concentrate lithium ions, while temperature-dependent conformational changes dynamically regulate ion transport pathways to maintain conductivity across extreme temperatures.
transfers.required_translation: Hydrophilic gel → thermoresponsive copolymer (e.g., PNIPAM-co-acrylic acid) with tunable LCST/UCST; osmotic pressure → Donnan potential from fixed anionic groups (sulfonate/carboxylate) on polymer backbone; fluid (water) → non-flammable liquid electrolyte (LiPF6 in fluoroethylene carbonate/dimethyl carbonate) or ionic liquid; evaporation gradient → temperature-driven decomposition/volatilization gradient; temporal aperture regulation → autonomous polymer chain collapse/swelling at phase transition temperatures; regulatory energy → thermal energy (passive) or applied potential (active gating).
transfers.expected_effect: Electrolyte maintains ≥10 mS/cm ionic conductivity from -40°C to 80°C, suppresses thermal decomposition and volatilization at 80°C (≤5% mass loss after 100h), prevents freezing at -40°C, achieves 4.5V electrochemical stability, and enables graphite/NMC compatibility with >99.5% Coulombic efficiency.
boundary_conditions: Polymer must be electrochemically inert up to 4.5V vs. Li/Li+
Phase transition temperatures tuned to -30°C (UCST) and 70°C (LCST) via copolymer composition
Fixed charge density ≥1.5 mol/L to generate sufficient Donnan potential for Li+ concentration
Mesh size in swollen state ≥2 nm for solvated Li+ transport; collapsed state ≤0.5 nm to block PF6- decomposition pathways
Mechanical modulus 1-10 MPa to withstand electrode volume changes
failure_conditions: Polymer oxidative degradation at cathode interface >4.3V
Phase transition hysteresis >10°C causing conductivity lag
Li+ transference number <0.4 due to anion trapping
Irreversible collapse from electrolyte syneresis after thermal cycling
Interfacial resistance >50 Ω·cm² at graphite anode
transfers.testable_prediction: A PNIPAM-co-sodium acrylate (85:15 mol%) hydrogel swollen with 1M LiPF6 in FEC:DMC (1:1) will exhibit a sharp conductivity drop from 12 mS/cm to 3 mS/cm at 65°C (LCST) with <2% electrolyte mass loss after 200h at 80°C, while maintaining 8 mS/cm at -40°C (UCST at -30°C), verified by in-situ EIS and TGA-MS during thermal cycling.
